atoms.direct_criterion: State separate exact valid-use domains for the crate-owned-implementation API and the generic external-implementation control.
Establish exact source selection and downstream accessibility for each submitted witness or control use.
Establish well-typedness, exact two-element array shapes, contextual usize typing of submitted index literals, coherence, and implementability of each complete use and trait implementation.
Establish that the exposed ordinary function call has no caller-side unsafe obligation and satisfy every other compiler-enforced unsafe-context obligation needed to form the use.
Keep the crate-owned unsafe impl's safety assertion inside the audited scope and do not assume it true when certifying the safe caller's valid use.

For the crate-owned invalid impl, prove array-to-slice method reachability, falsity of the exact in-scope assertion/in-bounds precondition, the applicable UB consequence, and the intended u8 dereference/copy result edge.
Issue the exact scoped UNSOUND verdict once the complete valid-use UB certificate closes.
Recognize that a downstream unsafe impl is an unsafe act whose implementer contract is owned outside the audited crate and must be satisfied for a valid-use witness.
Reject the submitted downstream impl that violates its unsafe implementer contract as a valid-use refutation, without using it to condemn the generic API.
Accept the contract-satisfying downstream unsafe impl as a valid control and prove its reached array-to-slice receiver, local in-bounds obligation, and u8 dereference/copy result.
Keep the crate-owned-invalid, downstream-invalid, and downstream-valid conclusions separate and reconcile every consumed Rust premise to exact Rust 1.83 authority.
